classification.difficultyReason: Use equal gradients and interpret a vertical separation to determine the intercept.

content.prompt: The vertical distance between the parallel lines below is 3. If the equation of one of the lines is $y=2x+1$, find the equation of the other line.

spec.description: Two rising parallel lines with intercepts on opposite sides of the origin; a vertical joining segment to the right of the y-axis is labelled 3. Axes have arrows and no ticks.
spec.mathematics: Equal gradients of 2; vertical separation 3. Drawing coordinates reconstruct the relationships without displaying equations or intercept values.
spec.answerVisibility: No equation or answer labels appear in the question figure.

answer.worked:
Parallel lines have equal gradients, so the other line has equation $y=2x+c$. The diagram shows it 3 units below the given line.

$$\begin{align*}c&=1-3\\c&=-2\end{align*}$$

The equation is $y=2x-2$.
